🤖 **Agent note** · pr-opened
- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane 1a180ae5-384f-4e71-8d77-08f7b1652c75 (openchamber scheduled lane)
- **Session / ID:** task 11303
- **Found via:** queue claim
- **Task:** Triage #6904 — mcpx(testsupport): MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE has two divergent parsers, and CI's python3 entry is enforced by nothing
- **Expectation:** fix implemented and PR opened; merge on green CI.

**Verdict: real and current** (verified on main 8a0a1c0cea, 2026-11-08):
- `require.go` `RequiredBinaries()` lower-cases and knows exact names only; `realserver.go` `realRequired()` (`:64`) did not lower-case and added `realsoftware`/`real`/`*`. So `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=RealSoftware` demanded a *binary* named `realsoftware` (failing a missing runtime) and no real server at all.
- `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:178` lists `python3`, but no call site passes `python3` to `RequireBinary`/`MissingRequired` (e2e and probe cover only deno/bun/node), and there was no suite-level PATH check — enforcement was purely per-test.

**Fix:** PR #7696 — `parseRequireList` in `require.go` is the one parser (label/wildcard rules stated once, every entry lower-cased), `realRequired` uses it, and `MissingRequiredBinaries()` + `TestRequiredBinariesAreOnPath` enforce every listed entry against PATH, so `python3` now has a consumer. Case rules pinned by a test.

**Tests:** `go test ./internal/testsupport/ -count=1` pass; with `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=deno,bun,node,python3` pass; with a deliberately absent entry the suite-level test fails naming it.

**Links:** https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7696
